_doc: Register of migration issues reviewed with Vincent (claude_doc/pg_migration.md § Step 2). Keys are issue ids from pg_migrate.py, fnmatch wildcards allowed. status: rule = handled by a conversion rule (say where) | accepted = harmless, reason given | fixed-data = corrected in HFSQL (seeing it again = REGRESSED). Every entry: status, decision, date.

nul_as_null:*.decision: R1. A text value starting with a NUL byte is NULL: HFSQL stores empty memos and fixed texts that way, and the MPS API already reads them as NULL (hfsql-bridge.ts cleanRow). Rule in hfsql_dump.c.

zero_date_null:*.decision: R2. An empty HFSQL date (all zeros) is NULL; PostgreSQL has no zero date. Rule in hfsql_dump.c.

integer_widening.decision: R3 (no issue id, documentation only). HFSQL integers can be unsigned (ref_echantillon.jauge = 65535 in a 2-byte column): every integer column is created one size up (2-byte -> integer, 4-byte -> bigint). pg_migrate.py TYPE_MAP.

skipped_backup:*.decision: R4. HFSQL lists its own backup copies (_backup/Sauvegarde des données de …) as tables of the database; they are never migrated. pg_migrate.py main loop.

renamed_column:*.decision: D2. Accented HFSQL names become unaccented lowercase in PostgreSQL. Column names come from the catalog (SQLColumns), the SELECT * header mangles some of them on this driver.

changed_during_copy:*.decision: The nightly copy reads a LIVE HFSQL; a table written during the copy (the TRS collector writes evenement_machine all night) differs by a few rows. On D-Day HFSQL is locked before the copy, so this cannot happen.
